components.note: 犭 (dog, beast) — animals: 狗, 猫, 狼; 独 first meant a solitary animal, then alone.
The old sound part 蜀 (shǔ) is also in 属 shǔ, 烛 zhú and 触 chù; simplified 独 shows 虫 instead.
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 她喜欢周末一个人在家独处。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zhōumò yī gè rén zàijiā dúchǔ.
example.english: She likes being alone at home by herself on weekends.
example.fact: Christopher Knight lived alone in the Maine woods for 27 years without a single conversation with another person, surviving through quiet, careful burglary of nearby cabins for food and supplies, until he was finally caught in 2013 — one of the most extreme documented cases of long-term solitude.

examples.hanzi: 有时候我需要一些时间独处。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu shíhou wǒ xūyào yīxiē shíjiān dúchǔ.
examples.english: Sometimes I need some time to be alone.

examples.hanzi: 独处并不等于孤独。
examples.pinyin: Dúchǔ bìng bù děngyú gūdú.
examples.english: Being alone does not mean being lonely.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.
月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.

example.hanzi: 他持有这家公司百分之十的股份。
example.pinyin: Tā chíyǒu zhè jiā gōngsī bǎi fēn zhī shí de gǔfèn.
example.english: He holds ten percent of the shares in this company.
example.fact: The Louvre Museum's most famous painting, the Mona Lisa, has been owned by the French state since the 16th century and is legally inalienable — a special law makes it, and other pieces in French national collections, permanently prohibited from being sold or given away.

examples.hanzi: 你持有有效的签证吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chíyǒu yǒuxiào de qiānzhèng ma?
examples.english: Do you hold a valid visa?

examples.hanzi: 很多人持有不同的看法。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō rén chíyǒu bùtóng de kànfǎ.
examples.english: Many people hold different views.

components.note: 南 (nán) — south; as a part it sounds out 楠 nán and 喃 nán.
瓜 (melon) — a melon hanging from a vine. It lends its sound to 孤 gū and 狐 hú, besides 傻瓜 and 南瓜.

example.hanzi: 每年秋天他们都会做南瓜派。
example.pinyin: Měinián qiūtiān tāmen dōu huì zuò nánguā pài.
example.english: Every autumn they make pumpkin pie.
example.fact: The largest pumpkin ever officially weighed, grown in Minnesota in 2023, tipped the scales at over 2,700 pounds — roughly the weight of a small car — and giant-pumpkin growers achieve such sizes partly by removing all but one fruit per vine so it receives the plant's entire energy supply.

examples.hanzi: 南瓜汤是我们家秋天常喝的汤。
examples.pinyin: Nánguā tāng shì wǒmen jiā qiūtiān cháng hē de tāng.
examples.english: Pumpkin soup is what our family often drinks in autumn.

examples.hanzi: 万圣节的时候，孩子们会雕刻南瓜灯。
examples.pinyin: Wànshèngjié de shíhou, háizimen huì diāokè nánguā dēng.
examples.english: At Halloween, kids carve pumpkin lanterns.

components.note: 力 (strength) — hard-won merit; also in 努 strive, 动 move. The traditional 勳 had 熏 xūn for the sound; 员 is only a stand-in.
音 (sound) — 音 over 十 — a full piece of music, so a section; 章 sounds out 彰 zhāng and 障 zhàng.

example.hanzi: 这位老兵胸前挂着好几枚勋章。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎobīng xiōngqián guà zhe hǎojǐ méi xūnzhāng.
example.english: This veteran had several medals hanging on his chest.
example.fact: The Medal of Honor, the United States' highest military decoration, has been awarded fewer than 3,600 times since its creation in 1861; each medal is individually cast, and by law it can never be bought or sold, only issued directly by the government.

examples.hanzi: 他因为勇敢救人获得了一枚勋章。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yǒnggǎn jiù rén huòdé le yī méi xūnzhāng.
examples.english: He received a medal for bravely saving someone's life.

examples.hanzi: 这枚勋章是国家颁发的最高荣誉。
examples.pinyin: Zhè méi xūnzhāng shì guójiā bānfā de zuìgāo róngyù.
examples.english: This medal is the highest honor awarded by the state.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.

example.hanzi: 她大学毕业后成为了一名会计。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu chéngwéi le yī míng kuàijì.
example.english: After graduating from university, she became an accountant.
example.fact: Double-entry bookkeeping, the accounting method still used worldwide today, was first systematically described in 1494 by Italian friar Luca Pacioli, sometimes called the 'father of accounting,' in a mathematics textbook that also happened to include the first published rules of the game we now know as blackjack.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司的会计每个月都要对账。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī de kuàijì měi gè yuè dōu yào duìzhàng.
examples.english: Our company's accountant reconciles the accounts every month.

examples.hanzi: 她在大学里学的是会计专业。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué lǐ xué de shì kuàijì zhuānyè.
examples.english: She studied accounting at university.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 墙上挂着一张全家的相片。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yī zhāng quánjiā de xiàngpiàn.
example.english: A photograph of the whole family hangs on the wall.
example.fact: The oldest surviving photograph of a person, taken by Louis Daguerre around 1838 on a Paris street, shows a man having his shoes shined; he appears only because he stood still long enough during the several-minute exposure, while everyone else walking by moved too fast to be captured.

examples.hanzi: 这张相片是我们去年在海边拍的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng xiàngpiàn shì wǒmen qùnián zài hǎibiān pāi de.
examples.english: This photo was taken at the seaside last year.

examples.hanzi: 请把相片发到我的邮箱里。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xiàngpiàn fā dào wǒ de yóuxiāng lǐ.
examples.english: Please send the photos to my email.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun sinking into the grass: dusk (the original of 暮 mù); later borrowed for "no, do not". 莫 also sounds out 墓 mù, 幕 mù and 摸 mō.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.
禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 科 first meant grading grain with a measure 斗, and then categories like 科学.
斗 (dipper) — 斗 is a measuring dipper, as in 斗 (a unit of grain).

example.hanzi: 莫斯科是俄罗斯的首都。
example.pinyin: Mòsīkē shì Éluósī de shǒudū.
example.english: Moscow is the capital of Russia.
example.fact: The Moscow Metro, opened in 1935, is famous for stations built like underground palaces, with marble columns, mosaics, and chandeliers; Mayakovskaya station is decorated with 34 ceiling mosaics depicting the sky at different times of day, designed partly to double as an air-raid shelter during World War II.

examples.hanzi: 我下个月要坐飞机去莫斯科出差。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xià gè yuè yào zuò fēijī qù Mòsīkē chūchāi.
examples.english: Next month I'm flying to Moscow on a business trip.

examples.hanzi: 莫斯科的冬天又长又冷。
examples.pinyin: Mòsīkē de dōngtiān yòu cháng yòu lěng.
examples.english: Winters in Moscow are long and cold.

meanings: to ride (in a train or other vehicle)

components.note: 乘 (chéng) — to ride; as a part it sounds out 剩 shèng.
土 (earth) — two people 从 sitting on the ground 土: to sit. Also in 座 zuò seat.

example.hanzi: 我们乘坐火车去了上海。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chéngzuò huǒchē qù le Shànghǎi.
example.english: We took a train to Shanghai.
example.fact: The Shanghai Maglev Train, which uses magnetic levitation to float above its track without touching it, can reach speeds of up to 268 miles per hour, making the roughly 19-mile trip from downtown Shanghai to Pudong International Airport in under eight minutes.

examples.hanzi: 请乘坐三号线地铁到市中心。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng chéngzuò sān hào xiàn dìtiě dào shì zhōngxīn.
examples.english: Please take Metro Line 3 to the city center.

examples.hanzi: 乘坐飞机前，要先办理登机手续。
examples.pinyin: Chéngzuò fēijī qián, yào xiān bànlǐ dēngjī shǒuxù.
examples.english: Before boarding a plane, you must check in first.

components.note: 示 (altar) — marks gods, rites and blessings, as in 神 god, 礼 ritual, 福 blessing; 祭 is offering meat on the altar, as in 祭祀.

example.hanzi: 清明节我们去祭拜祖先。
example.pinyin: Qīngmíng jié wǒmen qù jìbài zǔxiān.
example.english: On Qingming we go to pay respects to our ancestors.
example.fact: 祭 shows up in 祭祖 (ancestor worship), 祭品 (offerings), 祭坛 (altar). As a surname it is read Zhài.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末回乡下祭祖。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò huí xiāngxia jìzǔ.
examples.english: We are going back to the countryside this weekend to honor our ancestors.

examples.hanzi: 人们在这里举行祭祀活动。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen zài zhèlǐ jǔxíng jìsì huódòng.
examples.english: People hold ritual ceremonies here.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 浅 is shallow water.
戋 (jiān) — same sound: 浅 qiǎn/jiān. 戋 also sounds out 钱 qián, 线 xiàn and 盏 zhǎn.

example.hanzi: 这条河很浅，孩子也能走过去。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé hěn qiǎn, háizi yě néng zǒu guòqù.
example.english: This river is shallow; even a child could wade across.
example.fact: 浅 is the opposite of 深. It describes colours (浅蓝 light blue), and ideas (肤浅 superficial, 浅显 easy to grasp).

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服的颜色太浅了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de yánsè tài qiǎn le.
examples.english: The color of this garment is too light.

examples.hanzi: 他对这个问题的了解还很浅。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège wèntí de liǎojiě hái hěn qiǎn.
examples.english: His understanding of this problem is still superficial.

components.note: 页 (head) — heads and faces, as in 头, 题, 顶: to turn the head and look.
厄 stands in for 雇 (gù) in the traditional 顧; the clue is only loose today.

example.hanzi: 她一个人照顾三个孩子。
example.pinyin: Tā yí gè rén zhàogù sān gè háizi.
example.english: She looks after three children on her own.
example.fact: 顾 appears in 照顾 (take care of), 顾客 (customer), 回顾 (look back) and 顾虑 (misgiving).

examples.hanzi: 你别只顾着玩手机。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié zhǐgù zhe wán shǒujī.
examples.english: Don't just keep playing on your phone.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的顾客很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de gùkè hěn duō.
examples.english: This shop has many customers.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
扌 (hand) — shaking by hand; also in 摇 shake, 拍 pat.
斗 (dǒu) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 她冷得浑身发抖。
example.pinyin: Tā lěng de húnshēn fādǒu.
example.english: She was shivering all over from the cold.
example.fact: Shivering is the body's way of generating heat through rapid, involuntary muscle contractions, and it can boost metabolic heat production by up to five times the resting rate — though it's so energy-intensive that prolonged shivering can exhaust a person's glycogen reserves within about 15 to 20 minutes.

examples.hanzi: 他吓得浑身发抖，说不出话来。
examples.pinyin: Tā xià de húnshēn fādǒu, shuō bù chū huà lái.
examples.english: He trembled all over with fear and couldn't speak.

examples.hanzi: 她的声音因为紧张而发抖。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēngyīn yīnwèi jǐnzhāng ér fādǒu.
examples.english: Her voice shook with nervousness.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — oldest form: a person bending over a basin of water to see a reflection; 鉴 jiàn (mirror) adds metal. To look closely, to supervise.
目 (eye) — marks seeing and watching, as in 看, 眼, 睡; 督 is to oversee, to watch over.
叔 (shū) is a loose hint for dū.

example.hanzi: 工程建设过程需要专人监督。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéng jiànshè guòchéng xūyào zhuānrén jiāndū.
example.english: The construction process needs to be supervised by a dedicated person.
example.fact: The International Atomic Energy Agency, founded in 1957, sends inspectors to nuclear facilities in over 180 countries to monitor and verify that nuclear materials are not being diverted toward weapons programs, using tools ranging from surveillance cameras to tamper-proof seals on equipment.

examples.hanzi: 家长要监督孩子完成作业。
examples.pinyin: Jiāzhǎng yào jiāndū háizi wánchéng zuòyè.
examples.english: Parents should supervise their children in finishing homework.

examples.hanzi: 公众有权监督政府的工作。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzhòng yǒu quán jiāndū zhèngfǔ de gōngzuò.
examples.english: The public has the right to oversee the government's work.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — a hill is an obstacle, which fits 阻 to block; compare 院 courtyard, 陆 land.
且 (qiě) gives only a loose hint, but 阻 sounds exactly like 祖 zǔ and 组 zǔ, which share the same 且 part.
石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破 break, 码, 砖 brick; a stone in the road is an obstacle.

example.hanzi: 语言不通阻碍了双方的交流。
example.pinyin: Yǔyán bùtōng zǔ'ài le shuāngfāng de jiāoliú.
example.english: The language barrier hindered communication between the two sides.
example.fact: The Great Barrier Reef off the coast of Australia stretches over 1,400 miles and is large enough to be seen from space, yet rising ocean temperatures have caused repeated mass coral bleaching events since 2016, obstructing the reef's ability to recover between heat waves.

examples.hanzi: 大雪阻碍了交通，路上堵了很久。
examples.pinyin: Dàxuě zǔ'ài le jiāotōng, lùshang dǔ le hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: Heavy snow hindered traffic, causing a long jam on the road.

examples.hanzi: 不要让害羞阻碍你交朋友。
examples.pinyin: Bù yào ràng hàixiū zǔ'ài nǐ jiāo péngyou.
examples.english: Don't let shyness hold you back from making friends.

meanings: (of a system or device) to start operating automatically

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
户 (door) — 户 is a door with 口 below — 启 is opening; the traditional 啓 added a hand.

example.hanzi: 这项发明开启了人类通信的新时代。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng fāmíng kāiqǐ le rénlèi tōngxìn de xīn shídài.
example.english: This invention opened up a new era of human communication.
example.fact: Samuel Morse's first public long-distance telegraph message, sent in 1844 between Washington, D.C. and Baltimore, read 'What hath God wrought' — a message that took mere seconds to transmit over 38 miles of wire and helped open the era of near-instant long-distance communication.

examples.hanzi: 请按这个按钮开启电视。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng àn zhège ànniǔ kāiqǐ diànshì.
examples.english: Please press this button to turn on the TV.

examples.hanzi: 新学期开启了他生活的新篇章。
examples.pinyin: Xīn xuéqī kāiqǐ le tā shēnghuó de xīn piānzhāng.
examples.english: The new semester opened a new chapter in his life.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 秋, 种, 租; 称 originally meant weighing grain, then naming (称呼).
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 这种现象在物理学中被称作量子纠缠。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng xiànxiàng zài wùlǐxué zhōng bèi chēngzuò liàngzǐ jiūchán.
example.english: This phenomenon is called quantum entanglement in physics.
example.fact: Albert Einstein famously dismissed quantum entanglement as 'spooky action at a distance,' skeptical that particles could instantaneously affect one another across vast distances. Decades later, experiments confirmed entanglement is real, and the physicists who demonstrated it won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics.

examples.hanzi: 这种面食在北方被称作饺子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng miànshí zài běifāng bèi chēngzuò jiǎozi.
examples.english: This kind of pasta is called jiaozi in the north.

examples.hanzi: 人们把这座山称作"神山"。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen bǎ zhè zuò shān chēngzuò "shénshān".
examples.english: People call this mountain the "sacred mountain."

components.note: 先 (xiān) is only a loose clue; 宪 simplifies the traditional 憲.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 美国宪法于1787年制定。
example.pinyin: Měiguó xiànfǎ yú 1787 nián zhìdìng.
example.english: The US Constitution was drafted in 1787.
example.fact: The Constitution of San Marino, a tiny microstate inside Italy, is considered by some historians to be the oldest still-functioning written constitution in the world, with roots tracing back to statutes written in 1600, predating the US Constitution by nearly two centuries.

examples.hanzi: 每个公民都必须遵守宪法。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè gōngmín dōu bìxū zūnshǒu xiànfǎ.
examples.english: Every citizen must abide by the constitution.

examples.hanzi: 宪法保护公民的基本权利。
examples.pinyin: Xiànfǎ bǎohù gōngmín de jīběn quánlì.
examples.english: The constitution protects citizens' basic rights.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.
具 (tool) — two hands 廾 (the bottom 八) hold something valuable above — to provide, and a tool, as in 工具; 具 also sounds out 惧 jù.

example.hanzi: 演员在舞台上使用了很多道具。
example.pinyin: Yǎnyuán zài wǔtái shàng shǐyòng le hěn duō dàojù.
example.english: The actors used many props on stage.
example.fact: The lightsabers used throughout the original Star Wars trilogy were built around the flash handles of 1970s-era Graflex camera flash units, a prop-department improvisation that has since become one of the most recognizable pieces of movie weaponry in film history.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏里有很多可以收集的道具。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì lǐ yǒu hěn duō kěyǐ shōují de dàojù.
examples.english: This game has many items you can collect.

examples.hanzi: 剧组花了很多钱制作电影里的道具。
examples.pinyin: Jùzǔ huā le hěn duō qián zhìzuò diànyǐng lǐ de dàojù.
examples.english: The crew spent a lot of money making props for the film.

components.note: 疋 (foot, 足 variant) — clearing a channel so it flows; 疏 also sounds out 蔬 shū.
攵 (tap, strike) — marks actions, as in 教, 改, 放; 散 is to scatter (sàn) or to be loose (sǎn).

example.hanzi: 台风来临前,居民被紧急疏散到安全地带。
example.pinyin: Táifēng láilín qián, jūmín bèi jǐnjí shūsàn dào ānquán dìdài.
example.english: Before the typhoon arrived, residents were urgently evacuated to safe areas.
example.fact: Ahead of Hurricane Rita in 2005, roughly 2.5 million people evacuated the Houston area over a few days, creating gridlock so severe that some drivers spent more than 24 hours covering under 100 miles — a scale of movement that later reshaped how Gulf Coast cities plan hurricane evacuations.

examples.hanzi: 发生火灾时，大家要有秩序地疏散。
examples.pinyin: Fāshēng huǒzāi shí, dàjiā yào yǒu zhìxù de shūsàn.
examples.english: When a fire breaks out, everyone must evacuate in an orderly way.

examples.hanzi: 警察负责疏散广场上的人群。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá fùzé shūsàn guǎngchǎng shàng de rénqún.
examples.english: The police are in charge of dispersing the crowd in the square.

components.note: 走 (run, walk) — movement: 起 rise, 越 cross, 赶 hurry, 趣; 超 is to jump over, surpass.
召 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 招 zhāo, 绍 shào, 照 zhào.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行的花费超出了我们的预算。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng de huāfèi chāochū le wǒmen de yùsuàn.
example.english: The cost of this trip exceeded our budget.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House was originally budgeted at about 7 million Australian dollars in 1957 but ended up costing roughly 102 million dollars by its 1973 completion — a cost overrun of more than 1,300% that remains one of the most famous in architectural history.

examples.hanzi: 这个价格超出了我的预期。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiàgé chāochū le wǒ de yùqī.
examples.english: This price is beyond my expectations.

examples.hanzi: 他的能力远远超出了同龄人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nénglì yuǎnyuǎn chāochū le tónglíngrén.
examples.english: His ability far exceeds that of his peers.

components.note: 幺 (a tiny thread) — small and slight, as in 幻, 幽.
力 (strength) — little strength: the young; also in 努 strive, 动 move.
禾 (grain) — young crops, hence childlike; also in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
隹 (zhuī) is a rough clue; it also appears in 谁, 难, 集.

example.hanzi: 他觉得那种想法太幼稚了。
example.pinyin: Tā juéde nà zhǒng xiǎngfǎ tài yòuzhì le.
example.english: He felt that kind of thinking was too childish.
example.fact: Baby elephants suck their trunks the way human infants suck their thumbs, a self-soothing behavior researchers have observed particularly when a calf is stressed, hungry, or separated from its mother, showing that even large, intelligent animals retain distinctly juvenile comfort habits.

examples.hanzi: 你都二十岁了，别这么幼稚。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ dōu èrshí suì le, bié zhème yòuzhì.
examples.english: You're already twenty, so don't be so childish.

examples.hanzi: 这种幼稚的游戏只适合小孩子玩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yòuzhì de yóuxì zhǐ shìhé xiǎo háizi wán.
examples.english: This kind of childish game is only suitable for little kids.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh/body radical (月 in 脸, 脚, 肚); 背 is the back of the body.
北 (běi) — near sound — 背 is bèi; 北 originally pictured two people back to back, which is the sense of 背.
勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.

example.hanzi: 他背着一个大背包去旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā bēi zhe yī gè dà bēibāo qù lǔxíng.
example.english: He traveled carrying a large backpack.
example.fact: Ötzi the Iceman, a naturally mummified body from around 3,300 BC found frozen in the Alps in 1991, was discovered carrying a wood-framed backpack made of hazel and larch branches — making it one of the oldest known examples of a human carrying gear in a pack.

examples.hanzi: 我的背包里装着笔记本和水瓶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de bēibāo lǐ zhuāng zhe bǐjìběn hé shuǐpíng.
examples.english: My backpack holds a notebook and a water bottle.

examples.hanzi: 这个背包又轻又结实，很适合爬山。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bēibāo yòu qīng yòu jiēshi, hěn shìhé páshān.
examples.english: This backpack is light and sturdy, great for hiking.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a path under the foot; 歧 is a fork in the road, as in 步 step, 走.
支 (zhī) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 枝 zhī, 肢 zhī and 岐 qí.
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.

example.hanzi: 这部法律旨在消除职场中的性别歧视。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù fǎlǜ zhǐzài xiāochú zhíchǎng zhōng de xìngbié qíshì.
example.english: This law aims to eliminate gender discrimination in the workplace.
example.fact: The US Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlawed employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin; the inclusion of 'sex' was reportedly added late in the legislative process by an opponent hoping to sink the bill, yet the act passed and became a landmark of American law.

examples.hanzi: 我们不应该歧视任何人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù yīnggāi qíshì rènhé rén.
examples.english: We should not discriminate against anyone.

examples.hanzi: 她在找工作时遇到了年龄歧视。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhǎo gōngzuò shí yùdào le niánlíng qíshì.
examples.english: She faced age discrimination when job-hunting.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌: 极 first meant a roof beam, the very top.
及 (jí) gives the exact sound; also in 级 jí and 吸 xī.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and boundaries, as in 院, 陆, 阶; 限 is a limit.
艮 (gèn) is only a loose hint for xiàn; 根 gēn and 跟 gēn share it.

example.hanzi: 登山者挑战了人类体能的极限。
example.pinyin: Dēngshānzhě tiǎozhàn le rénlèi tǐnéng de jíxiàn.
example.english: The climber challenged the limits of human physical endurance.
example.fact: At the summit of Mount Everest, roughly 29,032 feet above sea level, air pressure is only about a third of that at sea level, meaning each breath delivers roughly a third of the oxygen — a physiological extreme so severe that the zone above 26,000 feet is nicknamed the 'death zone.'

examples.hanzi: 跑完马拉松已经到了他的体力极限。
examples.pinyin: Pǎo wán mǎlāsōng yǐjīng dào le tā de tǐlì jíxiàn.
examples.english: Finishing the marathon brought him to his physical limit.

examples.hanzi: 极限运动常常伴随着危险。
examples.pinyin: Jíxiàn yùndòng chángcháng bànsuí zhe wēixiǎn.
examples.english: Extreme sports often come with danger.

components.note: 凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 他一棒击球,把球打出了场外。
example.pinyin: Tā yī bàng jīqiú, bǎ qiú dǎ chū le chǎngwài.
example.english: He hit the ball with one swing, knocking it out of the park.
example.fact: A Major League Baseball pitch can leave a bat and travel back toward the pitcher's mound at over 100 miles per hour, giving the pitcher roughly four-tenths of a second to react — less time than it takes to blink twice — which is why comebacker line drives are considered uniquely dangerous.

examples.hanzi: 球员击球的动作非常标准。
examples.pinyin: Qiúyuán jīqiú de dòngzuò fēicháng biāozhǔn.
examples.english: The player's batting motion is very textbook.

examples.hanzi: 他在击球前先深吸了一口气。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jīqiú qián xiān shēn xī le yī kǒu qì.
examples.english: He took a deep breath before hitting the ball.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言, as in 说, 话, 请; 诺 is a spoken promise.
若 (ruò) — near sound — 诺 is nuò; 若 also sounds out 惹 rě.
亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.

example.hanzi: 诺亚方舟的故事家喻户晓。
example.pinyin: Nuòyà fāngzhōu de gùshì jiāyùhùxiǎo.
example.english: The story of Noah's Ark is well known to every household.
example.fact: The Epic of Gilgamesh, a Mesopotamian poem recorded on clay tablets around 2100 BC, contains a flood narrative strikingly similar to the biblical story of Noah — a man named Utnapishtim builds a boat to save his family and animals from a divine flood. Many scholars believe the biblical account and the Gilgamesh flood story share a common origin in even older Sumerian flood traditions from the Tigris-Euphrates river valley, a region prone to catastrophic flooding.

examples.hanzi: 诺亚造了一艘大船，带着动物们躲过了洪水。
examples.pinyin: Nuòyà zào le yī sōu dà chuán, dài zhe dòngwùmen duǒguò le hóngshuǐ.
examples.english: Noah built a big boat and took the animals to escape the flood.

examples.hanzi: 我女儿的英文名字叫诺亚。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǚ'ér de Yīngwén míngzi jiào Nuòyà.
examples.english: My son's English name is Noah.

components.note: 灬 (fire, 四点底) — flames below, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 煮 cook.
前 (qián) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 剪 jiǎn.
饣 (food) — 饣 is the simplified 食 (food), as in 饭, 饺, 饿; 饼 is a flat baked cake.
并 (bìng) — near sound — 饼 is bǐng; 并 also sounds out 拼 pīn.

example.hanzi: 妈妈早上给我做了煎饼当早饭。
example.pinyin: Māma zǎoshang gěi wǒ zuò le jiānbǐng dāng zǎofàn.
example.english: Mom made jianbing for me as breakfast this morning.
example.fact: The golden-brown crust that forms when a batter like jianbing hits a hot pan is caused by the Maillard reaction, a chemical reaction between amino acids and sugars first described by French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard in 1912. It's the same reaction responsible for the flavor of seared steak, toasted bread, and roasted coffee beans, and it only kicks in above roughly 140°C (280°F).

examples.hanzi: 街边的煎饼摊每天早上都排长队。
examples.pinyin: Jiēbiān de jiānbǐng tān měitiān zǎoshang dōu pái cháng duì.
examples.english: The street jianbing stall has a long line every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我要一个煎饼，加两个蛋，不要辣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào yī gè jiānbǐng, jiā liǎng gè dàn, bù yào là.
examples.english: I'd like a jianbing with two eggs, not spicy.

components.note: 气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 生日派对上挂满了五颜六色的气球。
example.pinyin: Shēngrì pàiduì shàng guà mǎn le wǔyánliùsè de qìqiú.
example.english: The birthday party was decorated with balloons of all colors.
example.fact: In June 1783, French brothers Joseph-Michel and Jacques-Étienne Montgolfier launched the first public demonstration of an unmanned hot air balloon in Annonay, France. Just months later, in November 1783, they sent the first humans aloft in a balloon flight over Paris, launching the era of human flight decades before the airplane.

examples.hanzi: 小朋友松手后，气球飞上了天空。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyou sōngshǒu hòu, qìqiú fēi shàng le tiānkōng.
examples.english: After the child let go, the balloon floated into the sky.

examples.hanzi: 他用嘴吹起了一个大气球。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng zuǐ chuī qǐ le yī gè dà qìqiú.
examples.english: He blew up a big balloon with his mouth.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
二 (two) — two parallel strokes: the next step after 一 and before 三.

example.hanzi: 我们每个星期二都有游泳课。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měi gè xīngqī'èr dōu yǒu yóuyǒng kè.
example.english: We have swimming class every Tuesday.
example.fact: In English, Tuesday is named after Tiw (or Tyr), the Norse god of war and justice, echoing the Roman naming of the day after Mars, the god of war (reflected in the French mardi and Spanish martes). The seven-day week itself traces back to ancient Babylon, which associated each of the seven visible 'planets' — including the sun and moon — with its own day.

examples.hanzi: 星期二下午我有一个很重要的会议。
examples.pinyin: Xīngqī'èr xiàwǔ wǒ yǒu yī gè hěn zhòngyào de huìyì.
examples.english: I have a very important meeting on Tuesday afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 今天是星期二，不是星期三。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì xīngqī'èr, bù shì xīngqīsān.
examples.english: Today is Tuesday, not Wednesday.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.hanzi: 那位老师教得非常认真。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi lǎoshī jiāo de fēicháng rènzhēn.
example.english: That teacher teaches very conscientiously.
example.fact: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088 in Italy, is generally considered the oldest continuously operating university in the world. It began as a student-run guild that hired its own teachers, a structure almost the reverse of a modern university, where the institution hires the faculty.

examples.hanzi: 那位先生是我们的新校长。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi xiānsheng shì wǒmen de xīn xiàozhǎng.
examples.english: That gentleman is our new principal.

examples.hanzi: 请问，那位穿红衣服的小姐是谁？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, nà wèi chuān hóng yīfu de xiǎojiě shì shéi?
examples.english: Excuse me, who is that lady in red?

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 电脑死机了，我只好从头再做一次。
example.pinyin: Diànnǎo sǐjī le, wǒ zhǐhǎo cóngtóu zài zuò yí cì.
example.english: The computer crashed, so I had to start over from the beginning.
example.fact: Many older computer systems store time as a 32-bit signed integer counting seconds since January 1, 1970 — a scheme that will overflow at 03:14:07 UTC on January 19, 2038, an event engineers call the 'Year 2038 problem.' It's a direct descendant of the Y2K bug, and some embedded systems with long service lives, like industrial controllers, are still being patched today to survive it.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌太好听了，我想从头再听一遍。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē tài hǎotīng le, wǒ xiǎng cóngtóu zài tīng yī biàn.
examples.english: This song is so nice that I want to listen from the beginning again.

examples.hanzi: 学外语要从头开始，一步一步来。
examples.pinyin: Xué wàiyǔ yào cóngtóu kāishǐ, yī bù yī bù lái.
examples.english: Learning a language requires starting from scratch, step by step.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — the visible frame, as in 原, 厚. Memory aid: a stern cliff face — 严重 serious, 严格 strict. Cliff family hint, not proven.
嚴 (traditional) — a larger shape with two mouths 吅 shouting orders. 严 cut it to 亚 plus 厂, losing the clue.
厂 (cliff) — stone and cliffs: 厚 thick, 原 origin, 压 press; 厉 first meant a whetstone, hence sharp and severe.

example.hanzi: 他对孩子的教育方式非常严厉。
example.pinyin: Tā duì háizi de jiàoyù fāngshì fēicháng yánlì.
example.english: His approach to educating his children is very strict.
example.fact: In the 1960s, developmental psychologist Diana Baumrind identified four parenting styles based on studies of preschoolers — authoritarian, authoritative, permissive, and neglectful — finding that children raised by strict but responsive 'authoritative' parents tended to fare better than those raised by harshly controlling 'authoritarian' ones. Her framework remains one of the most cited models in developmental psychology today.

examples.hanzi: 老师对作弊的学生非常严厉。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì zuòbì de xuésheng fēicháng yánlì.
examples.english: The teacher is very strict with students who cheat.

examples.hanzi: 他用严厉的语气批评了我。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng yánlì de yǔqì pīpíng le wǒ.
examples.english: He criticized me in a stern tone.

components.note: 去 (to go) — 丢 looks like 去 with an extra stroke on top. Memory aid: something that 'goes' away is lost.
厶 (private, small) — the lower part, as in 去. The dictionary story (a lost piece of jade 玉) is a later reading, not proven.
夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.

example.hanzi: 他的护照在旅途中不小心丢失了。
example.pinyin: Tā de hùzhào zài lǚtú zhōng bù xiǎoxīn diūshī le.
example.english: His passport was accidentally lost during the trip.
example.fact: Each year, airlines mishandle tens of millions of checked bags worldwide, though the rate has fallen sharply since the 2000s thanks to bar-coded tracking tags introduced across the industry. SITA's annual baggage report has tracked this decline, showing mishandling rates dropping from roughly 18 bags per 1,000 passengers in 2007 to under 6 by the late 2010s.

examples.hanzi: 如果行李丢失了，请马上告诉我们。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ xíngli diūshī le, qǐng mǎshàng gàosu wǒmen.
examples.english: If your luggage is lost, please tell us right away.

examples.hanzi: 这份文件丢失以后，公司很着急。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn diūshī yǐhòu, gōngsī hěn zháojí.
examples.english: After this document went missing, the company was very anxious.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 在中国文化中，面子是一个很重要的概念。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó wénhuà zhōng, miànzi shì yí gè hěn zhòngyào de gàiniàn.
example.english: In Chinese culture, 'face' is a very important concept.
example.fact: Sociologist Erving Goffman's 1955 essay 'On Face-Work' formalized the idea that all social interaction involves managing one's public image, or 'face' — a concept independently central to many cultures worldwide. Goffman argued that preserving face is a kind of unspoken ritual order that keeps everyday social encounters running smoothly.

examples.hanzi: 他很爱面子，从来不肯承认错误。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn ài miànzi, cónglái bù kěn chéngrèn cuòwù.
examples.english: He cares a lot about face and never admits his mistakes.

examples.hanzi: 看在我的面子上，原谅他这一次吧。
examples.pinyin: Kàn zài wǒ de miànzi shàng, yuánliàng tā zhè yī cì ba.
examples.english: For my sake, forgive him just this once.

components.note: 工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 这个城市因重工业而繁荣起来。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè chéngshì yīn zhònggōngyè ér fánróng qǐlái.
example.english: This city prospered because of heavy industry.
example.fact: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 18th century, powered initially by James Watt's improved steam engine, patented in 1769, which dramatically increased the efficiency of converting coal into mechanical work. Within a century, industrialization had transformed textile production, iron manufacturing, and transportation, reshaping the global economy and driving mass urban migration.

examples.hanzi: 这个地区的工业发展得很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū de gōngyè fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
examples.english: Industry in this region is developing quickly.

examples.hanzi: 工业污染让河水变得又脏又臭。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyè wūrǎn ràng héshuǐ biàn de yòu zāng yòu chòu.
examples.english: Industrial pollution made the river dirty and smelly.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.
力 (strength) — marks effort, as in 动 move, 努 strive, 办; 励 is to urge on.
厉 (lì) gives the sound exactly: 励 lì.

example.hanzi: 老师的鼓励激励了他继续努力学习。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī de gǔlì jīlì le tā jìxù nǔlì xuéxí.
example.english: The teacher's encouragement motivated him to keep studying hard.
example.fact: In 1714, the British Parliament established the Longitude Prize, offering up to £20,000 — a fortune at the time — to anyone who could devise a reliable way to determine a ship's longitude at sea. The prize spurred clockmaker John Harrison to spend decades perfecting the marine chronometer, a breakthrough that transformed ocean navigation.

examples.hanzi: 公司用奖金来激励员工努力工作。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yòng jiǎngjīn lái jīlì yuángōng nǔlì gōngzuò.
examples.english: The company uses bonuses to motivate employees to work hard.

examples.hanzi: 他的成功成了我们每个人的激励。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chénggōng chéng le wǒmen měi gè rén de jīlì.
examples.english: His success became a source of motivation for each of us.

components.note: 彳 (step, walk) — 彳 is the left-step radical, as in 行, 径, 德; 往 is going toward.
王 (wáng) — near sound — 往 is wǎng, same syllable with a different tone.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 往后我们要更加小心地处理这些数据。
example.pinyin: Wǎnghòu wǒmen yào gèngjiā xiǎoxīn de chǔlǐ zhèxiē shùjù.
example.english: From now on, we need to handle this data more carefully.
example.fact: The European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which took effect in May 2018, was one of the first laws to impose steep fines — up to 4% of a company's global annual revenue — for mishandling personal data. It has since influenced similar privacy laws in dozens of countries outside Europe, including Brazil, California, and India.

examples.hanzi: 往后的日子里，我们要互相照顾。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnghòu de rìzi lǐ, wǒmen yào hùxiāng zhàogù.
examples.english: In the days ahead, we should look after each other.

examples.hanzi: 请大家往后退一步，保持距离。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā wǎng hòu tuì yī bù, bǎochí jùlí.
examples.english: Everyone please take a step back and keep your distance.

components.note: 水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 那位水手在海上工作了三十年。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi shuǐshǒu zài hǎishàng gōngzuò le sānshí nián.
example.english: That sailor has worked at sea for thirty years.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind conducted one of the first controlled clinical trials, giving groups of scurvy-stricken sailors different remedies and finding that citrus fruit cured the disease fastest. It took the Royal Navy another 40 years to adopt his findings, but once it did, scurvy — which had killed more sailors than combat throughout the Age of Sail — largely disappeared from long voyages.

examples.hanzi: 水手们在甲板上拉紧了绳子。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐshǒumen zài jiǎbǎn shàng lā jǐn le shéngzi.
examples.english: The sailors tightened the ropes on the deck.

examples.hanzi: 我爷爷年轻的时候是一名水手。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye niánqīng de shíhou shì yī míng shuǐshǒu.
examples.english: My grandfather was a sailor when he was young.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胆 is the gall bladder, then courage.
旦 (dàn) hints at the sound: 胆 dǎn is close to 担 dān and 但 dàn.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子胆子很大。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi dǎnzi hěn dà.
example.english: This child is very bold.
example.fact: In Chinese, courage is 'a big gall bladder': 大胆 (bold), 胆小 (timid) and 胆子 (nerve). 卧薪尝胆 comes from the story of a king who tasted gall to remember his humiliation.

examples.hanzi: 他胆小，不敢一个人睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Tā dǎnxiǎo, bù gǎn yí ge rén shuìjiào.
examples.english: He is timid and dares not sleep alone.

examples.hanzi: 你真有胆量，敢去那座山。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn yǒu dǎnliàng, gǎn qù nà zuò shān.
examples.english: You are really brave to dare go up that mountain.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.
力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 劲 is energy and force.
又 (hand) — 又 here stands in for the older 巠, which gave the near sound: 经 jīng, 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 他使劲把门推开了。
example.pinyin: Tā shǐjìn bǎ mén tuī kāi le.
example.english: He pushed the door open with all his strength.
example.fact: The strongest muscle in the human body relative to its size is the masseter, the jaw muscle used for biting, which can exert a force of over 90 kilograms (200 pounds) at the molars in a forceful bite. Overall body strength, however, comes from the coordinated action of hundreds of muscles working together, not any single one.

examples.hanzi: 你再使劲一点，我们就能抬起来了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài shǐjìn yīdiǎn, wǒmen jiù néng tái qǐlái le.
examples.english: Push a bit harder and we can lift it.

examples.hanzi: 孩子使劲地喊着妈妈的名字。
examples.pinyin: Háizi shǐjìn de hǎn zhe māma de míngzi.
examples.english: The child shouted his mother's name with all his might.

components.note: 兼 (jiān) hints at the sound: 廉 lián is close to 镰 lián, 嫌 xián and 谦 qiān.
亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.

example.hanzi: 这家超市专门出售廉价商品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā chāoshì zhuānmén chūshòu liánjià shāngpǐn.
example.english: This supermarket specializes in selling low-cost goods.
example.fact: The standardized steel shipping container, introduced by American trucking entrepreneur Malcom McLean in 1956, cut the cost of loading cargo onto ships by roughly 90% compared to the older method of hand-loading loose freight. That single innovation is widely credited with making today's globally sourced, low-cost consumer goods economically possible.

examples.hanzi: 廉价的衣服穿几次就坏了。
examples.pinyin: Liánjià de yīfu chuān jǐ cì jiù huài le.
examples.english: Cheap clothes break after a few wears.

examples.hanzi: 这家旅馆房价廉价，很受学生欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā lǚguǎn fángjià liánjià, hěn shòu xuésheng huānyíng.
examples.english: This hotel's rooms are low-priced and popular with students.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a picture of an ear; as a radical it marks hearing, as in 闻, 聪, 聊.
王 (jade) — 王 on the left is 玉 (jade) as in 玩, 球, 现; 环 is a jade ring, as in 环境.

example.hanzi: 她今天戴了一对漂亮的耳环。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān dài le yí duì piàoliang de ěrhuán.
example.english: She wore a pair of beautiful earrings today.
example.fact: Ötzi the Iceman, a naturally mummified body found frozen in the Ötztal Alps in 1991 and dated to roughly 3300 BC, had earlobes stretched by earrings measuring 7 to 11 millimeters across — evidence that ear piercing is at least five millennia old. Archaeologists have found gold earrings from Mesopotamia dating back almost as far, showing the practice arose independently across several ancient cultures.

examples.hanzi: 她一边照镜子一边戴上了金耳环。
examples.pinyin: Tā yībiān zhào jìngzi yībiān dài shàng le jīn ěrhuán.
examples.english: She put on gold earrings while looking in the mirror.

examples.hanzi: 我不小心丢了一只耳环。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎoxīn diū le yī zhī ěrhuán.
examples.english: I accidentally lost one earring.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 会上，经理宣布了新的销售计划。
example.pinyin: Huì shang, jīnglǐ xuānbù le xīn de xiāoshòu jìhuà.
example.english: At the meeting, the manager announced the new sales plan.
example.fact: Robert's Rules of Order, first published in 1876 by U.S. Army officer Henry Martyn Robert, standardized how meetings and votes should be conducted and remains the most widely used parliamentary procedure manual in the English-speaking world. It was inspired by his frustration after presiding over a chaotic church meeting with no clear rules for debate.

examples.hanzi: 会上大家都发表了自己的看法。
examples.pinyin: Huì shang dàjiā dōu fābiǎo le zìjǐ de kànfǎ.
examples.english: At the meeting, everyone expressed their views.

examples.hanzi: 他在会上提出了一个很好的建议。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huì shang tíchū le yī gè hěn hǎo de jiànyì.
examples.english: He put forward a very good suggestion at the meeting.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).
贝 (shell, old money) — allowances and payments, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
占 (zhàn) is only a loose sound clue for tiē.

example.hanzi: 他是一个非常体贴的丈夫。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè fēicháng tǐtiē de zhàngfu.
example.english: He is a very considerate husband.
example.fact: Psychologist Daniel Goleman's 1995 book 'Emotional Intelligence' popularized the idea that skills like empathy and self-awareness matter as much as IQ for personal and professional success. The underlying academic concept had been introduced a few years earlier, in 1990, by psychologists Peter Salovey and John Mayer, who first defined and measured it scientifically.

examples.hanzi: 她对老人非常体贴，常常帮他们买菜。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì lǎorén fēicháng tǐtiē, chángcháng bāng tāmen mǎi cài.
examples.english: She is very considerate to the elderly and often buys groceries for them.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你这么体贴，还给我带了雨伞。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ zhème tǐtiē, hái gěi wǒ dài le yǔsǎn.
examples.english: Thank you for being so thoughtful and bringing me an umbrella.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 这个软件只支持特定的操作系统。
example.pinyin: Zhè gè ruǎnjiàn zhǐ zhīchí tèdìng de cāozuò xìtǒng.
example.english: This software only supports specific operating systems.
example.fact: Unix, the ancestor of Linux, macOS, and Android's core, was created in 1969 by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs, originally to run on a spare PDP-7 minicomputer after a bigger multi-user project called Multics was abandoned. Its design principles — small, modular programs that each do one thing well — still shape how operating systems are built more than fifty years later.

examples.hanzi: 只有特定的人才能进入这个房间。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu tèdìng de rén cái néng jìnrù zhège fángjiān.
examples.english: Only certain people can enter this room.

examples.hanzi: 这种药物在特定的条件下才有效。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yàowù zài tèdìng de tiáojiàn xià cái yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This drug works only under specific conditions.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — ear radical, as in 聪 clever, 聋 deaf, 闻 to hear.
止 (zhǐ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 址 zhǐ and 趾 zhǐ.
辱 (rǔ) — to humiliate; as a part it sounds out 褥 rù and 溽 rù.

example.hanzi: 战败对这支球队来说是巨大的耻辱。
example.pinyin: Zhànbài duì zhè zhī qiúduì lái shuō shì jùdà de chǐrǔ.
example.english: The defeat was a huge disgrace for this team.
example.fact: Article 231 of the 1919 Treaty of Versailles, often called the 'war guilt clause,' forced Germany to accept blame for World War I and pay reparations, a stipulation many Germans experienced as a profound national disgrace. Historians still debate how much that resentment contributed to the political instability that followed in the 1920s and 1930s.

examples.hanzi: 被人当众骂，他觉得是一种耻辱。
examples.pinyin: Bèi rén dāngzhòng mà, tā juéde shì yī zhǒng chǐrǔ.
examples.english: Being scolded in public felt like humiliation to him.

examples.hanzi: 他们终于洗刷了多年的耻辱。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhōngyú xǐshuā le duō nián de chǐrǔ.
examples.english: They finally wiped away years of disgrace.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.

example.hanzi: 小心，这种蘑菇是有毒的。
example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, zhè zhǒng mógu shì yǒudú de.
example.english: Be careful, this kind of mushroom is poisonous.
example.fact: The death cap mushroom (Amanita phalloides) is responsible for the majority of fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide, and it closely resembles several edible species, making misidentification easy. Its toxin, amatoxin, attacks the liver but produces no symptoms for 6 to 24 hours after ingestion, a delay that often leads victims to underestimate the danger until serious organ damage has already begun.

examples.hanzi: 这条河里的水有毒，不能喝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé lǐ de shuǐ yǒudú, bù néng hē.
examples.english: The water in this river is poisonous and undrinkable.

examples.hanzi: 有毒的气体会危害人的健康。
examples.pinyin: Yǒudú de qìtǐ huì wēihài rén de jiànkāng.
examples.english: Toxic gases harm people's health.

components.note: 氵 (water) — harbours lie on water; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
巷 (xiàng) shares the rhyme -ang; only a loose sound clue.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 上海是世界上最繁忙的港口之一。
example.pinyin: Shànghǎi shì shìjiè shàng zuì fánmáng de gǎngkǒu zhī yī.
example.english: Shanghai is one of the busiest ports in the world.
example.fact: The Port of Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port by cargo volume every year since 2010, handling over 47 million shipping containers in 2022 alone. Much of its capacity comes from the Yangshan Deep-Water Port, an artificial island connected to the mainland by a 32-kilometer bridge, built because the natural harbor near Shanghai was too shallow for the largest modern cargo ships.

examples.hanzi: 很多货船停在港口，等着卸货。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō huòchuán tíng zài gǎngkǒu, děng zhe xièhuò.
examples.english: Many cargo ships are docked at the port waiting to unload.

examples.hanzi: 我们坐船离开了这个小港口。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán líkāi le zhège xiǎo gǎngkǒu.
examples.english: We left this small harbor by boat.

components.note: 日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.hanzi: 跑步已经成了他日常生活的一部分。
example.pinyin: Pǎobù yǐjīng chéng le tā rìcháng shēnghuó de yí bùfen.
example.english: Running has become part of his daily life.
example.fact: In 2017, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to Jeffrey Hall, Michael Rosbash, and Michael Young for discovering the molecular mechanisms that control the circadian rhythm — the roughly 24-hour internal clock that governs daily patterns of sleep, hormone release, and body temperature in nearly all living organisms. Their research began with fruit flies and identified a specific gene, period, whose protein levels rise and fall in a daily cycle.

examples.hanzi: 这本书教你一些日常用语。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū jiāo nǐ yīxiē rìcháng yòngyǔ.
examples.english: This book teaches you some everyday phrases.

examples.hanzi: 日常的小事也要认真对待。
examples.pinyin: Rìcháng de xiǎo shì yě yào rènzhēn duìdài.
examples.english: Even small daily matters should be taken seriously.

components.note: 歹 (bone, death) — marks death and decay, as in 死 die, 殆; 残 is damaged or cruel.
戋 (jiān) is a loose hint for cán; it appears in 钱 qián, 浅 qiǎn and 线 xiàn.

example.hanzi: 他的腿有残疾。
example.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ yǒu cánjí.
example.english: He has a leg disability.
example.fact: 残 means damaged or remaining: 残疾 (disability), 残留 (residue), 残忍 (cruel), 残酷 (brutal). 残废 is now often considered impolite.

examples.hanzi: 这套茶具已经残缺不全了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào chájù yǐjīng cánquē bù quán le.
examples.english: This tea set is already incomplete.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位残疾运动员，拿了冠军。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi cánjí yùndòngyuán, ná le guànjūn.
examples.english: He is a disabled athlete who won the championship.
